items.title: First-play frame freezes: one 2.03–2.67 s freeze in combat per fresh browser, plus 145–297 ms frames at run start (GI.6: no frame > 100 ms after warm-up)
items.evidence: captures/gntcjourney4-trace8-prod-a/-b/-c/-w-p1.analysis.json. Fresh GPU-harness browser, only my chrome.exe running (9–12), real input through L1 rooms 1-8, the card and L2 rooms 1-2, 0 debug clears, p50 12.1 ms. Frames > 100 ms per trace: 3/4/3/4. Max frame: 2442.5 ms (L1 boss, 9 ticks before the Stag died), 2066.7 ms (L2 r1, 0.5 s after level_start), 2672.8 ms (L2 r1, 19 ticks after level_start), 2030.3 ms (L2 r2). Run-start frames: 145.5/260.4/260.7, 248.6/272.7, 151.5/296.9/278.8 ms. Other: 103 ms at shop open, 109.1 ms on the level_clear frame. During the freezes the page's 100 ms setInterval kept firing (15-16 samples with the tick frozen), no longtask was recorded, and GPU-3D use fell from 90-99% to the idle 25%. GL program and texture counts did not change. trace8-prod-w-p2 (same trace, same browser, warm): 0 frames > 100 ms, max 91 ms. So this is a first-use GPU-process cost that the boot warm-up does not cover.
items.reproduce: npm run build -- --outDir dist-gntcjourney4; ECHOES_NET_PORT=7851 npx vite preview --outDir dist-gntcjourney4 --port 4330; node tools/gntcjourney4-trace8.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:4330 --seed 7 --tag X (fresh browser, waits for 0 chrome.exe); node tools/gntcjourney4-trace8an.mjs captures/gntcjourney4-trace8-X.json → the .analysis.json lists every > 50 ms frame by phase. For the warm comparison: node tools/gntcjourney4-trace8w.mjs --passes 2
refuters:
This is a harness artifact. The 2–3 s freeze comes from a freshly launched headless GPU-harness browser: it happens once per browser, whether or not the game is running. It is not a first-use cost of Echoes content that the boot warm-up misses.

Evidence, all from my own runs:
(1) A plain WebGL2 page with no Echoes code at all (instanced quads, MSAA and 4 blur passes) froze once for 1835 ms, 119.6 s after launch. It had 0 other frames > 100 ms. At 119.9 s the browser started its DX12/Vulkan info-collection GPU process (--type=gpu-process --disable-gpu-sandbox --use-gl=disabled).

Verdict: most of J4-F1 is refuted, but a smaller part survives. The 2.03–2.67 s freezes (the headline) come from the harness browser, not the game. The 145–297 ms run-start frames are real and still fail GI.6, so the finding stays must-fix with a narrower scope.

items.title: Closing the tab mid-run loses completed rooms and the drafted build: a throttled room-entry autosave is dropped, never deferred, with no pagehide save and no leave prompt
items.evidence: captures/gntcjourney4-closeloss-prod-s7.json, all real input. auto-1 was written at room 1 entry (5764 ms). Room 1 cleared by real input in 13.2 s, draft lantern_flurry taken, door chosen. Room 2 entered at 20,520 ms, 14.8 s after the room-1 autosave, so it was throttled. No autosave was written for the next 35 s, although the party cleared room 2 at 34,263 ms. The tab was closed with runBeforeUnload and no dialog appeared. The title then showed Continue 'Level I · The Hollow Wood · Room 1 · just now · Autosave'. After Continue: skills went from [mending_bolt, swift_mend, lantern_flurry] to [mending_bolt, swift_mend], bench 2 to 0, Glint 12 to 0, sigEq false. Control run closeloss-prod-r2: room 1 took 18.5 s, room 2 came 20.0 s after the autosave, so it was saved and the build restored identically. In the five real-input G3 traces, room 2 came 14.7-18.4 s after room 1 (5/5 under 20 s) and room 3 came 12.9-20.5 s after room 2 (4/5 under). unload-prod.json: no onbeforeunload handler, nothing written on hidden or pagehide. This breaks PLAN §8 Save 'no lost progress' and Journey 'without … lost state'.
items.reproduce: With the preview on :4330: node tools/gntcjourney4-closeloss.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:4330 --tag X --seed 7 --stay 25000 --rooms 2 → C1 and C2 FAIL. By hand: fresh profile → New Game → portal E → clear room 1 quickly → take the draft → door → in room 2 close the tab → reopen → Continue says Room 1 with the old build

items.title: Host Quit to Lobby pulls the guest out of a Level-2 fight into camp with no notice
items.evidence: captures/gntcjourney4-mpnotice-prod.json leg N1 (zero-config through the preview proxy). A MutationObserver on the guest's whole body was armed before the host's action. After the host confirmed Quit to Lobby in L2 room 1, the guest's DOM gained only 'WAVE 1/2' (318 ms), the camp plate 'THE HEARTH CAMP · NIGHT · BEFORE THE ROAD' (1321 ms) and a ping, plus one event, return_to_camp (1293 ms). No toast, banner or card names the host, the quit or the lobby. gntcjourney4-mpnotice-prod-N1-guest-400/1500/4000.png show camp with only the 'Online · Tank Room DHEKB · 2 players' plate. For contrast, the host leaving does produce notices on the remaining client (N2/N2b), and a guest leaving is announced to the host (N3).
items.reproduce: node server/index.mjs --port 7851 behind ECHOES_NET_PORT=7851 npx vite preview --port 4330, then node tools/gntcjourney4-mpnotice.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:4330 --port 7851 --tag X → N1 FAIL. By hand: host and guest in a session, host Begin Run, reach Level 2, host Esc → Quit to Lobby → confirm, and watch the guest's screen
refuters:
J4-F3 reproduces on my own runs, so it is not a harness artifact. I varied the conditions the harness lens cares about:
(1) A fresh production build of the same bundle (version 0.5.124, entry index-DGyKhaqD.js) on my own vite preview :4347, proxied to my own session server :7874 with no ?net= (zero-config). addressInfo reports source 'site'.
(2) The live dev server :5199 with ?net= pointing at my own server :7875 (source 'param').
(3) Host and guest in two separate browser processes instead of two contexts of one browser. The guest's addressInfo showed hasFocus:true and visibility 'visible'.

- **L1:** the host pressed E at the portal and got to Level 1 room 1 combat without any debug skips.
